_doc: Every door input can arrive through for THIS loop. Read by ~/.claude/tools/comms.py, which counts and flags but never opens a message. A DECLARATION, not a router.
_no_addresses_here: This repo is PUBLIC. Queries are written as shapes and senders are named by role, never by address — the contact roster lives in `bolo-private/data/venue-contacts.json`. A declaration that leaks the thing it describes is a bad trade.

channels.name: gmail:band-availability
channels.query: prose replies to band-wide availability threads — /bolo-ingest owns the sender→roster-id mapping
channels.note: The band answering a date. Read by /bolo-ingest, which diffs against the attendance record and proposes gated writes.

channels.name: gmail:calendar-rsvp
channels.query: Google Calendar RSVP notification mail for band events
channels.note: ⚠️ An RSVP burst is often a calendar CLIENT re-syncing, not a decision. /bolo-ingest flags that shape; a counter here must not read a burst as N new answers.

channels.name: gmail:venue-outreach
channels.query: replies on booking threads — see bolo-private/data/venue-contacts.json for the roster
channels.note: Also the input to /check-contacts-drift, which reconciles last_contact_date against real send history.

channels.name: imessage:band group thread
channels.note: ⛔ THE KNOWN BLIND SPOT. Attendance also lives in an iMessage group and /bolo-ingest is Gmail-only — it CANNOT see it. The text sits in `attributedBody` and names resolve via AddressBook, so it is technically readable but nothing sweeps it today. A FRESH verdict on this loop never covers this door. (memory: reference_bolo_imessage_group_thread)

channels.name: phone / in-person at practice
channels.note: Availability and set decisions get settled at practice and reach the record only when Paul enters them.
